witnesses.title: nbformat-4.5-informed document fidelity check (FAILED attempt, superseded by W1-rev2)
witnesses.stderr_summary: TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int' - replay ordering sorted execution_count without handling the schema-defined null ('not been run') case
witnesses.expected_behavior_justification: schema [S4] defines execution_count as integer>=0 or null; the check itself was wrong to sort mixed values - the crash is evidence the replay-order rule must partition never-run cells
witnesses.scope_limits: schema-level rules only; does not run the real nbformat library

witnesses.title: bounded-memory streaming NDJSON transform with reject ledger
witnesses.stdout_summary: 50000 lines: 49997 ok + 3 rejected (ledger with line/byte_offset/reason/raw); sum preserved; max rows materialized 512 <= budget 1024; preview bounded to 5 and flagged sample-not-proof; unicode/null/missing/timestamp values exercised; source sha256 unchanged (read-only)
witnesses.expected_behavior_justification: brief requires bounded/streaming processing, no silent deletion of malformed records, no mutation of originals, preview not represented as full-dataset proof; each assertion maps to a contract rule (proposal 5 D1-D7)
witnesses.scope_limits: 50k-row in-memory synthetic corpus, not a 5 GB file; json.loads-per-line is not the production engine; memory bound is app-tracked, not OS-measured

witnesses.title: output-status invalidation state machine
witnesses.stdout_summary: 13-event scenario asserted: run/edit/dataset-change/error/re-run/kernel-restart; final statuses all unverified after restart; error marks cell failed + descendants unverified; dataset identity change stales readers transitively
witnesses.expected_behavior_justification: the brief's required invalidation semantics (upstream edit, source change, env change, restart, interrupt must never leave stale outputs labeled current); rules are the product choice formalized in proposal 6
witnesses.scope_limits: model-level simulation of a 3-cell DAG; no real kernel, no real editor; transitive-ancestor lookup recomputed per event

witnesses.title: clean-replay determinism + reproducibility manifest + nondeterminism exposure
witnesses.stdout_summary: pure transform replayed twice -> identical output bytes; unseeded random -> different values across runs (must be declared); manifest emitted with notebook hash, per-cell code hashes + exec order + status, dataset sha256/bytes/declared schema, python 3.14.4/Linux env binding, replay verdict
witnesses.expected_behavior_justification: brief requires a reproducibility manifest and an honest clean-replay boundary; identical bytes for pure code and differing bytes for unseeded RNG demonstrate both the guarantee and its stated limit
witnesses.scope_limits: no subprocess isolation (fresh state emulated); sandbox interpreter was 3.14.4 - not one of the proposed supported versions; manifest shape is illustrative, not a frozen schema
